security_spec.violation_condition: When V=1, if the hardware SPMP checker uses hspmpen bit[i] (the new hypervisor-level SPMP activation CSR) to gate SPMP entry i instead of spmpen, but the CSR module does NOT properly enforce that hspmpen[i] becomes read-only when spmpcfg[i].L==1 — OR symmetrically, when a vSPMP entry's vspmpcfg[i].L lock bit is set but the hardware fails to gate write-ignore behavior on V==1 (the spec now conditions lock enforcement on V==1), allowing a guest in VS-mode to bypass the lock by clearing V before writing — then the hypervisor's memory isolation is violated.
security_spec.summary: PR #90 renames hspmpswitch→hspmpen, introduces vspmpen, defines hspmpdeleg CSR bit layout, gates vSPMP lock on V=1, and mandates virtual-instruction exception on vSPMP CSR access when hstatus.VTVM=1/V=1 — hardware must ensure lock-bit write-protection is context-aware (V-dependent) and hspmpdeleg WARL clamping cascades correctly on mpmpdeleg writes

findings.finding: All Smpmpind indirect CSR data registers (mireg2-mireg6, sireg2-sireg6, vsireg2-sireg6) are ZeroFieldBundle stubs: regOut := 0.U, writes silently discarded. The Smpmpind indirect access path (miselect selects SPMP register set → mireg2-6 routes write to spmpcfg/spmpaddr entries) is entirely absent. No SPMP configuration or address CSR writes can reach any SPMP entry memory through the indirect CSR channel.
findings.snippet:
val mireg2 = Module(new CSRModule("Mireg2", new ZeroFieldBundle(...)) { regOut := 0.U }).setAddr(CSRs.mireg2)
val mireg3 = Module(new CSRModule("Mireg3", new ZeroFieldBundle(...)) { regOut := 0.U }).setAddr(CSRs.mireg3)
val mireg4 = Module(new CSRModule("Mireg4", new ZeroFieldBundle(...)) { regOut := 0.U }).setAddr(CSRs.mireg4)
val mireg5 = Module(new CSRModule("Mireg5", new ZeroFieldBundle(...)) { regOut := 0.U }).setAddr(CSRs.mireg5)
val mireg6 = Module(new CSRModule("Mireg6", new ZeroFieldBundle(...)) { regOut := 0.U }).setAddr(CSRs.mireg6)

findings.finding: All Smpmpind indirect CSR access is unconditionally blocked as illegal. rwMireg2_6_EX_II is always true regardless of privState or miselect value. rwSireg2_6_EX_II and rwVSireg2_6_EX_II similarly always trigger illegal-instruction exception for any access to sireg2-6 or vsireg2-6. No privilege mode (M/HS/VS) can access the SPMP indirect register window. The Smcsrind/Sscsrind instruction extension is explicitly not implemented (comment at line 257: 'Smcsrind/Sscsrind is not implemented').

miselect CSR only recognizes AIA ranges (0x30-0x3F) and IMSIC ranges (0x70-0xFF) as legal. All Smpmpind miselect values (which would be in ranges 0x00-0x2F or 0x40-0x6F for SPMP configuration/address sets) are classified as illegal via isIllegal detection. The MISelectField WARL constraint hardcodes these subranges as reserved. Consequently, no miselect value can select an SPMP register set for indirect access.
findings.snippet:
def isInAIA(iselect: UInt): Bool = iselect >= 0x30.U && iselect < 0x50.U
def isInImsic(iselect: UInt): Bool = iselect >= 0x70.U && iselect < 0x100.U
def isInOthers(iselect: UInt): Bool = !isInAIA(iselect) && !isInImsic(iselect)
def isIllegal(iselect: UInt): Bool = isInOthers(iselect) && iselect =/= 0.U

findings.finding: mseccfg.MMWP (bit 1) is hardcoded as RO (read-only zero), making it impossible to enable SPMP even if SPMP hardware existed. This is correct behavior for a system without SPMP but means the entire SPMP activation path (MMWP=1 → SPMP enabled for S-mode when mstatus.MPP != M) is absent. Without MMWP being writable, no SPMP entry can ever be activated for checking.
findings.snippet: val MMWP = RO(1, lit = 0.U).withReset(0.U)  // MMWP is read-only zero

findings.finding: menvcfg.SSE (bit 3) and senvcfg.SSE are hardcoded RO(0), permanently disabling S-mode access to the SPMP indirect CSR access window. With SSE=0, even if Smpmpind indirect registers existed, they would trap on S-mode access. This is correct for a system without SPMP, but confirms the complete absence of SPMP infrastructure.

Only M-mode pmpcfg0-pmpcfg3 (addresses 0x3A0-0x3A3) and pmpaddr0-pmpaddr63 (0x3B0-0x3EF) are instantiated. No SPMP configuration CSRs (spmpcfg0-spmpcfg15 at 0x1CC-0x1CF via SME select, or direct 0x1D0-0x1DF) exist. No SPMP address CSRs (spmpaddr0-spmpaddr63) exist. The PMPCfgBundle is 8-bit (R/W/X/A/ATOMIC/C/L) with no SPMP fields (SHARED, U, RWX[2:0], E). The CSR address constant definitions in CSRs.scala also contain no spmpcfg/spmpaddr entries.

Only the M-mode PMPChecker module exists. No SPMPChecker module is instantiated in parallel. The SPMP checker would need to: decode {SHARED, U, RWX, SUM} fields into access decisions per the SPMP encoding table; generate page-fault exception codes (12/13/15) instead of access-fault codes (1/5/7); consume mseccfg.MMWP and menvcfg.SSE for enablement gating; and produce independent exception signals that don't collide with PMP access-fault outputs.

location.function_name: PMPEntryHandleModule (spmpen/hspmpen/vspmpen enable + L-bit lock enforcement for SPMP)

findings.finding: Lock-bit enforcement exists only for M-mode PMP entries. No spmpen, hspmpen, or vspmpen CSR modules exist. No SPMP-specific lock enforcement logic exists. The security spec's violation condition — 'when spmpcfg[i].L==1 but hspmpen[i] is not properly gated write-ignore' — cannot be evaluated because neither the SPMP config registers, the SPMP enable registers, nor the lock enforcement logic exist in the RTL. When V=1, there is no hspmpen CSR to check, no vspmpcfg to validate, and no SPMP checker to bypass.

Only M-mode PMP parameters are configured (NumPMP=64, NumPMPReal=32, PlatformGrain). No SPMP-specific configuration parameters exist (e.g., NumSPMP for the number of SPMP entries, SPMPSupported flag, SPMPGrain for SPMP address granularity). All Chisel elaboration for SPMP hardware would be conditionally gated on such parameters; their absence means zero SPMP gates are synthesized.
